import pandas as pd


def run(inputs: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    events = inputs["events"].copy()
    
    # Sort by user_id, event_ts, event_id to establish the order
    events = events.sort_values(by=["user_id", "event_ts", "event_id"]).reset_index(drop=True)
    
    # For each user, compute the lag of event_ts
    events["prev_event_ts"] = events.groupby("user_id")["event_ts"].shift(1)
    
    # Compute the time difference in minutes
    events["time_diff_minutes"] = (events["event_ts"] - events["prev_event_ts"]).dt.total_seconds() / 60
    
    # A new session starts if:
    # 1. prev_event_ts is NULL (first event for a user), OR
    # 2. time_diff_minutes > 30
    events["new_sess"] = (events["prev_event_ts"].isna()) | (events["time_diff_minutes"] > 30)
    events["new_sess"] = events["new_sess"].astype(int)
    
    # Compute session_num as cumulative sum of new_sess within each user
    events["session_num"] = events.groupby("user_id")["new_sess"].cumsum()
    
    # Group by user_id and session_num to compute aggregates
    user_sessions = events.groupby(["user_id", "session_num"]).agg(
        session_start=("event_ts", "min"),
        session_end=("event_ts", "max"),
        event_count=("event_id", "count")
    ).reset_index()
    
    # Ensure session_num is int64
    user_sessions["session_num"] = user_sessions["session_num"].astype("int64")
    
    # Reorder columns
    user_sessions = user_sessions[["user_id", "session_num", "session_start", "session_end", "event_count"]]
    
    # Sort by user_id and session_num
    user_sessions = user_sessions.sort_values(by=["user_id", "session_num"]).reset_index(drop=True)
    
    return {"user_sessions": user_sessions}
